newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London weak on Wall Street gloom.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London weak on Wall Street gloom.

text.p: U.S. stocks in London were weaker on Friday, hit by profit-taking overnight on Wall Street and caution ahead of key U.S. durable goods figures, dealers said.

"The market's looking a bit weak this morning and we see further profit-taking. Bonds are down again and futures are pointing downwards, although there's not too much business around," one trader said.

Overnight, the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 43.98 points to 5,992.48 as profit-taking in oil stocks pulled the index below the key 6,000 level for the first time in two weeks. Dealers said that decline was likely to continue.
"We would need a real surprise on durable goods to stop the rot...even good corporate earnings fail to make an impact on this market," a second dealer said.
Consensus forecasts predict a 2.0 percent rise in durable goods orders in September although forecasts range between rises of 0.8 percent and 3.5 percent. The data is due at 1230 GMT.

Among movers in London, Procter & Gamble continued its decline, trading $1/4 lower at 93-3/4. The stock slipped in New York after the company reported record first-quarter earnings but a decline in worldwide sales.
Mobil lost $1/4 to $117 and Atlantic Richfield was down $3/8 at $132.
Boeing lost $1/4 to $95-1/4 despite reporting higher third quarter earnings on Thursday.

Dealers said the share was coming under pressure from reports investigators had found critical sections of jet fuel probes from the TWA Flight 800 crash which could help resolve whether the Boeing 747 suffered mechanical failure.
